definition: Machine learning with multi-layer neural networks that learn hierarchical representations from raw data.
details: By stacking many layers, deep networks compose simple features into increasingly abstract ones — edges into parts, parts into objects — with the representations learned from data rather than engineered. Combined with large datasets and fast GPUs, this approach reset the state of the art across speech, vision, translation and games.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. In plain words: Machine learning with multi-layer neural networks that learn hierarchical representations from raw data. Here is how it actually plays out: By stacking many layers, deep networks compose simple features into increasingly abstract ones — edges into parts, parts into objects — with the representations learned from data rather than engineered. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Deep Learning.
